Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with an atopic eczema (atopic dermatitis) flare:  
  - Past eczema history with worsening itchy, dry, sore rash typical of chronic atopic dermatitis affecting flexural areas (inside elbows, hands, chest)  
  - No systemic symptoms or signs of secondary infection identified on exam  
  - Lack of response to mild OTC hydrocortisone supports need for stronger topical steroid  
- Secondary bacterial infection is less likely given absence of weeping, crusting, fever, or scratch marks but cannot be completely excluded  
- Contact dermatitis possible but no recent changes in skin products reported  
- Steroid inadequacy likely contributing — current mild hydrocortisone cream insufficient for severe flare  
- Nutritional deficiency and other causes considered low likelihood based on history and exam  

Management Plan  
- Prescribed Fexofenadine (antihistamine) for itch relief  
- Initiated stronger topical steroid: Betnovate (very small amount, twice daily) for two weeks  
- Continue regular emollients (Diprobase cream and Dermal soap)  
- Monitor for adverse reactions or worsening symptoms; advised to seek earlier review if no improvement or worsening condition within two weeks  
- Prescription sent electronically to local Boots pharmacy for collection

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
- Atopic eczema (atopic dermatitis) flare – High likelihood  
  - Supported by history of eczema, rash distribution, and clinical presentation typical of flare without systemic signs  
- Secondary bacterial infection (impetiginization) of eczema – Moderate likelihood  
  - Worsening soreness and redness could indicate infection, but lack of weeping, crusting, or fever reduces probability  
- Contact dermatitis (irritant/allergic) – Moderate likelihood  
  - Possible but no reported new exposures or products making this less likely  
- Steroid inadequacy or resistance – Low likelihood  
  - Mild hydrocortisone ineffective, supporting need for stronger steroid but no signs of steroid-induced skin complications
